pulls.title: test: measure rpcwaittimeout floor with monotonic time
pulls.body:
Previously, `interface_bitcoin_cli.py` measured the `-rpcwaittimeout` wait floor with `time.time()`. `bitcoin-cli` arms that deadline with `std::chrono::steady_clock`, so a CI wall-clock step backward can make the elapsed time look short and cause the assert to fail.

Fix this by using `time.monotonic()` instead and using `-rpcwaittimeout=1`. The log line also now says "at least" so it matches the floor assert.

h/t ViniciusCestarii for suggesting `time.monotonic()` here.

pulls.title: bugfix: send shortened IPv6 addresses to SOCKS5 proxies in full
pulls.body:
Found while auditing #36628 

Already known upstream issue with C-tor: https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor/-/issues/32314

With `-proxy` pointed at Tor, outbound connections to IPv6 peers whose
 address contains an inner `::` always fail with "general failure".

 Core sends every SOCKS5 destination as a DOMAINNAME, with IPv6 in its
 compressed form. Tor copies the name into its relay BEGIN cell as
 `<name>:<port>`, and the exit's `tor_addr_port_split` first tries to parse
 the whole string as an IPv6 address. `2001:db8::1:8333` is a valid one,
 because the `::` absorbs the port as an eighth group. The exit then sees no
 port and closes the stream. Addresses written with all eight groups, or
 ending in `::`, are unaffected: appending `:port` to them does not give a
 valid address.

 About 20% of the IPv6 addresses in a gossip-filled addrman, and 29% of
 current IPv6 DNS seed answers, have an inner `::`. The failure is closed;
 there is no fallback to a direct connection.

 Note that this also effects private broadcast by default.

 This PR sends such addresses with all eight groups written out
 (`2001:db8:0:0:0:0:0:1`). `<name>:<port>` then has nine groups, so the exit
 splits at the last colon. Other forms:

 | Form                  | Tor         | Tor, SafeSocks 1 | getaddrinfo-based proxies |
 |-----------------------|-------------|------------------|---------------------------|
 | `2001:db8::1` (today) | fails       | fails            | works                     |
 | `[2001:db8::1]`       | works       | works            | fails                     |
 | ATYP IPv6             | works, logs a DNS-leak warning | refused | works         |
 | eight groups (this PR)| works       | works            | works                     |

 Tested against tor 0.4.9.13: on mainnet, master could not reach four
 seed-provided peers with inner-`::` addresses (30 "general failure"); with
 this change all four connected and completed the version handshake.
 `feature_proxy.py` and a new `netbase_tests` case check the bytes sent.

pulls.body:
Most supported operating systems ship with clang-19 (or later), so bump the minimum to that and allow new code to drop workarounds for previous clang bugs.

(For this bump, only C++20 CTAD will become available.)

This patch will only be released in version 33.x, next year (2027).

For reference:

* https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/clang-22
* https://packages.ubuntu.com/noble/clang-20
* CentOS-like 8/9/10 ship clang-21 via Stream
* Free/Open/Net*BSD ship clang-19
* OpenSuse Tumbleweed ships with https://software.opensuse.org/package/clang (clang22); leap:latest with clang-19
* macOS 14: depends/release cross-builds are unaffected and use clang-19
* macOS 14: Native builds use llvm-19-ish via XCode CLT 26.3 since https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36287

* https://packages.ubuntu.com/jammy/g++-12
* https://apt.llvm.org/, brew, nix, guix, or compile clang from source, ...

pulls.title: torcontrol: escape backslashes in -torpassword
pulls.body:
With `HASHEDPASSWORD` authentication, `TorController::protocolinfo_cb` sends the password as a quoted string, `AUTHENTICATE "<password>"` (torcontrol.cpp:667). It escapes `"` but not `\`.

Tor parses that argument as a control-spec QuotedString, where a backslash escapes the next character. So:

- `-torpassword=pa\ss` reaches Tor as `pass`, authentication fails and no onion service is created
- `-torpassword=pass\` escapes the closing quote, so the command is malformed

This escapes backslashes before quotes.

The new `test_password_escaping` in `feature_torcontrol.py` uses the mock control server with `HASHEDPASSWORD` and `-torpassword=pa\ss"word\`, and checks the exact `AUTHENTICATE` line. On master it gets `AUTHENTICATE "pa\ss\"word\"`, with the fix `AUTHENTICATE "pa\\ss\"word\\"`.

Tested against Tor 0.4.9.12 with `HashedControlPassword` set for `pa\ss"word\`: on master bitcoind logs "tor: Authentication failed", with this change authentication succeeds and ADD_ONION creates the onion service.

AI tools were used to help find this issue and to prepare the patch and test.

pulls.title: rpc: Properly throw on internal I/O errors in GetTransaction
pulls.body:
Currently the GetTransaction return value is a nullable transaction
pointer, where nullptr represents two different outcomes: I/O error and
missing tx.

Reporting a confirmed transaction as missing is wrong, so properly
return an error instead.
